It supports the intellectual, personal, and professional development of its Majors, Minors, and Graduate students by preparing students for life, leadership, and careers in a changing, multicultural world through the process of learning and application in a polytechnic university setting. Critical thinking and analytical reasoning is encouraged at all levels and quantitative analysis using current tools and methods emphasized. The Department provides a learning opportunity for students in an environment of collegiality, collaboration, and enthusiasm for learning within the local as well as the global community. The Department of Economics provides a flexible, interdisciplinary education grounded in economic theory and quantitative analysis. The curriculum supports both professional preparation and academic advancement, offering pathways to careers in the private and public sectors as well as graduate study in economics, business, law, public policy, and data science. Faculty integrate applied learning and research to ensure that students develop strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills that are valued across industries and disciplines. courses.title: Contemporary Economic Issues
courses.description: [GE 4A] Introduction to economic issues. Use of basic economic theories to explain current and future events. Themes may cover international, social, or election year topics. Investigation of a specific economic issue by an individual or as part of a group. Open to non-economics and non-business majors.
courses.prerequisites: Open to non-economics and non-business majors.

courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.description: [GE 4A] Fundamentals of microeconomics. Economic examination of problems of choice among alternative allocations, utilizations, and distributions of resources. Market analysis, consumer and firm behavior, market structure, externalities, and welfare economics.

courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.description: [GE 4A] Introduction to macroeconomics. Determinants of national income, output, and price levels. Monetary and fiscal policy. International economics. Applications of economic principles to domestic and international problems.

courses.title: Economic Statistics
courses.description: Statistical methods and techniques in economic analysis. Analysis of time series, index number construction, regression and correlation analysis, probability and other statistical distributions; related economic topics. Corequisite(s): EC 3322A .

courses.title: Economic Statistics Activity
courses.description: Hands-on experience with statistics in economics. Students will conduct and interpret appropriate statistical tests and will learn how to use statistical software such as R and Excel. Corequisite(s): EC 3322 .

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; and Instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of demand and supply. Consumer choice analysis. Income and substitution effects. Firm profit maximization and industry structure. Economic efficiency and welfare effects of policy instruments. Corequisite(s): EC 4401A .

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics Activity
courses.description: Applications of demand and supply. Consumer choice analysis applications. Applications of firm profit maximization and industry structure. Economic efficiency and welfare effects of policy applications. This course focuses on demonstrating applications of theory in intermediate economics to facilitate learning modeling techniques used throughout the economics major. Corequisite(s): EC 4401 .

courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Overview of the micro foundations of macroeconomic models and use of these models to understand decisions of consumers, firms, and the government. Includes study of labor market dynamics and wages. Measurement of national accounts and the determinants of economic growth.

courses.title: International Economics
courses.description: Analysis of international income, trade, and financial asset streams. Role of exchange rate dynamics, balance of payments, international financial systems, tariffs and quotas on economic growth and welfare.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201, and EC 2202 or EC 220; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Mathematical Economics
courses.description: Mathematical description and derivation of micro- and macroeconomic theory.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; EC 2202 or EC 220; and MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 1250 or MAT 125; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: History of Economic Thought
courses.description: History of the development of economic ideas and doctrines from Greek writers through the classical and neoclassical schools to the present.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Money and Banking
courses.description: Nature and functions of money and its relation to interest, output and prices; the monetary system of the United States; structure and functions of the Federal Reserve System; economic impacts of banks, bank credit and monetary control.

courses.title: Economic Development
courses.description: Historical, contemporary, and comparative examination of economic development and growth of developing countries. Issues include poverty, income inequality, population growth, urban-rural migration, environmental, health and education problems, and economic approaches to address them.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Public Finance
courses.description: Principles of government financing and its economic and social effects. Analysis of collection, spending, and administration of public funds.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; or Graduate standing.

courses.title: Urban Economics
courses.description: Historical to contemporary analysis of the economic growth and development of cities. Location theory. Examination of theoretical and policy approaches to resolve urban problems in labor markets, education, physical and social infrastructure, land use, crime, environmental issues, and housing.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; or Graduate standing.

courses.title: Labor Economics
courses.description: Structure and theory of labor markets. Role of government policy in labor markets. Evaluation and analysis of theoretical models of wage determination under different market structures, discrimination, migration, and job amenities. Analysis of labor market data with current software.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 1250 , MAT 125, EC 322, EC 3322 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Sports Economics
courses.description: Economic models of the structure of sporting markets, and the interaction of such markets with local governments. Empirical analysis utilizing publicly available data to test economic theories, e.g. wage determination.

courses.title: Environmental Economics
courses.description: Examination of the relationship between economic theory, environmental problems, and economic institutions. Theory of externalities and market failure. Historical to contemporary market and government approaches to manage air, water, solid and hazardous waste issues.

courses.title: Economics of Marriage and the Family
courses.description: Analysis of economic theories of marriage formation and dissolution, household fertility decisions, household bargaining, and labor force participation. Examination of gender discrimination in the workforce and inequality.

courses.title: Industrial Organization
courses.description: Evaluation and analysis of government regulation of the private sector aimed at creating a more competitive economy. Analysis of models of imperfect competition among strategic firms including, but not limited to, quantity competition, price competition, and monopoly pricing models.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 1250 or MAT 125; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Industry Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C or 5D] Examination of the historical, scientific, technological, and economic developments of a selected industry. Domestic and international market analysis. Impact of regulations and laws on industry operations. Selected industries may include: health care, airlines, entertainment, wine, computer systems, steel, automobiles, biotechnology. May be taken unlimited times only with different topics.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Countrywide Economic Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Socioeconomic aspects of a country, or countries, and their social, economic, and political relationship with the United States. Topics include the targeted country or countries’ economic growth, trade, socioeconomic issues, and its relationship to the United States.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Introduction to econometrics, with a focus on understanding and applying the classical linear regression model; emphasis placed on applications of regression analysis; quantitative model-building; estimation, verification, and prediction of economic variables. Corequisite(s): EC 4444A .

courses.title: Econometrics Activity
courses.description: Hands-on experience with statistics in economics. Students will conduct and interpret appropriate statistical tests and will learn how to use R and R-studio. Corequisite(s): EC 4444 .

courses.title: Economic Forecasting
courses.description: Techniques and applications of statistical analysis of macroeconomic and microeconomic conditions. Analysis of trends and cycles. Problem-solving, forecasting, and evaluation using econometric and time-series models. Integration of generative AI tools for programming assistance, visualization, and portfolio analysis.

courses.title: Economic Programming and Optimization Analysis
courses.description: Economic optimization analysis and programming techniques, including linear and nonlinear methods. Case studies, deterministic model-building. Computer applications of optimization analysis.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; and EC 4406 or EC 406; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Economic Research
courses.description: Dual Listed as: EC 5558 Introduces the fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence, including Machine Learning and Generative AI, without requiring advanced mathematics such as Calculus or Matrix Algebra. Using the statistical software R for hands-on examples, explore practical applications of AI techniques such as Random Forest, k-Nearest Neighbors, Neural Networks, and Generative AI for economic research. Bridges basic theory and practice in preparation to apply AI tools effectively and responsibly for economic problems such as predicting individual employment or predicting asset prices. Will also cover the limitations of AI use. Corequisite(s): EC 4447A .
courses.prerequisites: EC 3322 , STA 1200 , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Economic Research Activity
courses.description: Dual Listed as: EC 5558A Emphasizes the practical application of AI and Machine Learning from an economics framework. Complete assignments that strengthen technical and analytical skills. Provides intensive instructor guidance to support the design and implementation of data science applications in economics. Semester concludes with a project that integrates concepts into the analysis of an economic problem. Present findings in a quantitative project report. Corequisite(s): EC 4447 .
courses.prerequisites: EC 3322 , STA 1200 , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Spatial Econometrics
courses.description: Econometric analysis of spatial distance and location on economic growth, taxation, optimization, and social issues. Topics include spatial economic suitability analysis, spatial approximation, and clustering of economic phenomena, as well as spatial correlation of economic variables.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: Introduction to game theoretic approaches, particularly simultaneous and sequential games, games with Nash equilibria and Prisoners’ Dilemma, coordination games, uncertainty, and strategic moves. Develop strategic thinking skills by applying game theoretic approaches to economics, business, politics, psychology and legal problems.

courses.title: Capital Markets
courses.description: Monetary theory and capital markets; intensive focus on theoretical and mathematical tools necessary for analysis of banks and other financial institutions, and the effectiveness of monetary policy.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; and EC 4408 or EC 408; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Gambling, Risk and Information
courses.description: Economics of risk, uncertainty, and information. Economic inquiry into gambling, insurance, asset pricing, and related topics involving risky decisions. Role of information in improving choices involving risk.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or E3B/C202; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Applied Economic Research
courses.description: Development of critical inquiry skills for economic analysis. Application of economic research methods to develop testable implications. Conduct tests of previously untested theories and interpret results relative to existing findings within economic and social science literature.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; and EC 2202 or EC 202; or Graduate standing.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Applications of the various techniques of economic analysis to issues and topics in economics, broadly defined. Perform economic research and write original economic research paper. Research topics must be approved by instructor. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: EC 3322 , EC 4401 , EC 4403 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Graduate Microeconomics Preparation
courses.description: Calculus based presentation of microeconomic theory including consumer and producer theory.

courses.title: Graduate Quantitative Preparation
courses.description: Introduction to advanced probability, statistical, and quantitative methods used in advanced theoretical and applied econometrics.

courses.title: Graduate Macroeconomics Preparation
courses.description: Introduction to modern theoretical macroeconomic models, their microfoundations, and applications.

courses.title: Microeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Calculus and set theory based presentation of microeconomic theory including consumer and producer theory as well as general equilibrium models.

courses.title: Macroeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of aggregate national economic activities using dynamic models.
courses.prerequisites: EC 4403 or EC 403; and EC 5503 or EC 503.

courses.title: Graduate Econometrics I
courses.description: Specification and statistical inference in econometric models; estimation, verification and prediction of economic variables; recent empirical studies, advanced topics in econometrics.

courses.title: Graduate Econometrics II
courses.description: Specification and statistical inference in econometric models; estimation, verification and prediction of economic variables; recent empirical studies, advanced topics in econometrics.

courses.title: International Finance
courses.description: Advanced topics in international liquidity and finance theory. Problems of international monetary systems. Balance of payments theory and practices; theory of exchange rates and mechanism of international adjustment.

courses.title: Capital Markets I
courses.description: Topics in monetary and capital theory. Liquidity creation, financial intermediation and capital formation. Development of capital policy.

courses.title: Capital Markets II
courses.description: Topics in monetary and capital theory. Liquidity creation, financial intermediation and capital formation. Development of capital policy.

courses.title: Graduate Public Finance
courses.description: Public policies, principles, and standards of taxation and expenditures, budgeting, public goods, income redistribution, regulation, and development. Examine the equity and efficiency of public policy and assess the fiscal impact.

courses.title: Graduate Research Practicum I
courses.description: Intensive study of applied research methods and technical writing through replication of existing peer-reviewed findings in the economics literature or through selected research topics determined by the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: EC 5550 or EC 550; and EC 5551 or EC 551; and EC 5503 or EC 503.

courses.title: Graduate Research Practicum II
courses.description: Intensive study of applied research methods and technical writing through replication of existing peer-reviewed findings in the economics literature or through selected research topics determined by the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: EC 5550 or EC 550; and EC 6692 or EC 692.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Independent research and study under the supervision of the faculty. Reporting the research results in the approved form. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 12 units. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and Graduate Writing Assessment passed*.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
